title: AWS/GCP Marketplace Vendor Account Access & Credential Rotation (Vendor Management Process)
author: Olga Petrov
related_pages: ADR: Marketplace SKU naming and entitlement IDs (confluence:architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-marketplace-sku-naming-and-entitlement-ids)
body:
## 1. Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference’s standard process for managing access to the AWS Marketplace and GCP Cloud Marketplace vendor/producer portals, including:
- Who is allowed to access vendor portals and submit listing changes.
- Minimum security requirements (MFA, device posture, audit trail expectations).
- Credential management and rotation (passwords, API tokens where applicable, backup codes).
- Offboarding, periodic access reviews, and break-glass procedures.

This process exists to reduce the risk of unauthorized marketplace listing changes, fraud (banking/payout modifications), and accidental submission of incorrect security/compliance claims.

## 2. Scope
### In scope
- AWS Marketplace / Partner portals used to manage Redwood’s marketplace listings and seller profile.
- GCP Cloud Marketplace Producer Portal and associated partner tooling.
- Any credentials, shared resources, or privileged access used to submit or approve listing changes.

### Out of scope
- Customer-facing onboarding flows (purchase → entitlement → org linking). See the marketplace onboarding design spec and engineering runbooks.
- Redwood internal access controls (Console roles, billing systems) except where required for marketplace change approval workflows.

## 3. Systems covered
We maintain access controls for the following vendor systems (names may vary by vendor UI):
- **AWS**: AWS Marketplace Management Portal, AWS Partner Central (as applicable for listing assets/support), seller profile settings.
- **GCP**: Cloud Marketplace Producer Portal, Partner Advantage / Partner portal pages used for submission and communications.

Note: Vendor portals sometimes change branding and menu structure. Requirements and controls in this document apply regardless of UI label.

## 4. Guiding principles
1) **Least privilege**: Only grant access needed for the role (copy-only vs pricing/SKU vs seller profile/payout).
2) **No shared personal accounts**: Each user must have an individually attributable vendor identity wherever the vendor supports it.
3) **MFA required**: All vendor access must use strong MFA (see Section 6).
4) **Auditability**: We must be able to reconstruct “who changed what and when” for listings and seller configuration.
5) **Separation of duties**: High-risk actions (pricing/SKU changes; payout/banking changes; publishing) require at least one approver outside the requestor’s function.

## 5. Roles, permissions, and who can submit changes
### 5.1 Role definitions
Because AWS/GCP portals differ, we use Redwood role categories and map to vendor capabilities:

**A) Marketplace Submitter (Full)**
- Can submit listing changes for review/publish (including product packages/SKUs where portal supports it).
- Can upload required security documentation for review cycles.
- Cannot change payout/banking details unless explicitly designated (see Role D).

**B) Marketplace Submitter (Copy/Assets)**
- Can edit draft listing copy, upload screenshots, and update metadata (categories/keywords).
- Cannot change pricing/SKUs or publish without a Full Submitter.

**C) Marketplace Admin (Technical/Integration)**
- Can manage technical integration settings tied to marketplace provisioning/webhooks (if present in vendor tooling).
- Can view submission status and technical validation errors.
- Cannot approve/alter security claims without Security sign-off.

**D) Seller Profile / Finance Admin (High Risk)**
- Can modify seller profile details, payout/banking/tax settings, and legal contacts.
- Access is tightly restricted and requires Finance + Legal approval.

### 5.2 Authorized personnel (current)
Access is granted by named individual and reviewed quarterly.

**Primary Marketplace Submitters (Full)**
- Soojin Lee (Product Marketing Lead)
- Talia Benson (Engineering Program Manager) — operational backup during active refresh windows

**Marketplace Submitters (Copy/Assets)**
- Camila Reyes (Marketing Executive Sponsor)

**Marketplace Admin (Technical/Integration)**
- Ethan Park (Engineering Lead, control plane entitlement mapping)
- Connor O'Brien (Release Engineering)

**Seller Profile / Finance Admin (High Risk)**
- Laura Bennett (Finance Sponsor) — delegated operator
- Michael Grant (Legal Sponsor) — approval-only unless emergency

**Security approvers (required for security packet language/evidence)**
- Dr. Aisha Rahman (Security Executive Sponsor/sign-off)
- Marcus Lin (Security Engineering Lead)
- Olga Petrov (GRC Lead)

If an individual is not listed above, they are not authorized to submit or approve marketplace changes without an access request and review.

### 5.3 Approval requirements by change type
**Copy/screenshots/keywords**
- Required: PMM (Soojin Lee) + Marketing (Camila Reyes) review.
- Submission: Copy/Assets Submitter or Full Submitter.

**SKU taxonomy, pricing, metering, legal terms references**
- Required: Product owner (Nikhil Sharma / Lauren Bishop / Vivek Kulkarni depending on SKU) + Finance (Laura Bennett) + Legal (Michael Grant).
- Submission: Full Submitter.

**Security/compliance statements and attachments**
- Required: Security (Dr. Aisha Rahman or Marcus Lin) + GRC (Olga Petrov).
- Submission: Full Submitter; upload may be performed by Security/GRC if portal access is granted.

**Seller profile / payout/banking / tax settings**
- Required: Finance (Laura Bennett) + Legal (Michael Grant) + Security (Dr. Aisha Rahman).
- Submission: Seller Profile / Finance Admin only.

## 6. MFA and device requirements
### 6.1 MFA policy
All vendor portal access must use MFA with the following priority:
1) **FIDO2/WebAuthn security key** (preferred) registered to the vendor account.
2) **TOTP authenticator** (Okta Verify / Google Authenticator) if security keys are not supported.
3) SMS-based MFA is **not allowed** except where vendor limitation exists and Security explicitly approves an exception.

### 6.2 Backup codes and recovery
- Backup codes (if provided by the vendor) must be stored in the approved secrets manager vault (see Section 7) under restricted access.
- Do not store backup codes in email, Slack, or shared Google Docs.

### 6.3 Device posture
- Access vendor portals only from company-managed devices with full-disk encryption and screen lock enabled.
- Browser password saving is disabled for marketplace credentials.

## 7. Credential storage and handling
### 7.1 Approved storage
- All non-SSO vendor credentials and backup codes must be stored in **1Password** in the vault: **“Partner Portals (Restricted)”**.
- Access to this vault is limited to authorized roles above and is audited.

### 7.2 Prohibited handling
- No credentials in Slack, email, or ticket comments.
- No screenshotting of MFA QR codes.
- No exporting vendor credential lists for “convenience.”

### 7.3 Password requirements
- Minimum 20 characters, randomly generated.
- Unique per vendor portal.
- Rotation cadence depends on risk tier (Section 8).

## 8. Rotation cadence
### 8.1 Rotation tiers
**Tier 1 (High risk): Seller profile / payout / banking / tax**
- Rotate passwords: every **60 days**.
- Re-validate MFA methods: every **60 days**.
- Access review: quarterly.

**Tier 2 (Standard): Listing submission / draft edits / publishing**
- Rotate passwords: every **90 days**.
- MFA validation: every **90 days**.
- Access review: quarterly.

**Tier 3 (Low risk / view-only where supported)**
- Rotate passwords: every **180 days**.
- Access review: quarterly.

### 8.2 Rotation ownership
- **GRC (Olga Petrov)** owns the rotation calendar and evidence collection.
- **Security Eng (Marcus Lin)** owns exception review and approval for vendor limitations.
- **Partnerships/PMM (Soojin Lee)** owns ensuring rotations do not block time-sensitive submissions.

## 9. Access request and provisioning process
All new access requests must be tracked in the internal support system.

### 9.1 When to request access
Examples:
- New backup submitter needed for a submission deadline.
- Engineering needs portal access to address technical validation issues.
- Finance admin needed for payout/tax updates.

### 9.2 How to request access
1) File a request in **INT-332 (or create a new Internal Support ticket under Vendor Access)**.
2) Include:
   - Vendor portal(s): AWS, GCP, or both.
   - Requested Redwood role category (Section 5.1).
   - Business justification and time window.
   - Required approvers (based on change type).
   - Confirmation the user has a registered security key (preferred) or approved TOTP.
3) Required approvals:
   - Standard access (Tier 2/3): Soojin Lee + Olga Petrov.
   - High-risk access (Tier 1): Laura Bennett + Michael Grant + Dr. Aisha Rahman.

### 9.3 Provisioning steps (operator checklist)
1) Confirm approvals are present in the ticket.
2) Create or invite the user in the vendor portal using their corporate email.
3) Assign minimum vendor permissions to match the role category.
4) Require MFA enrollment at first login.
5) Record the following in the ticket (do not include secrets):
   - Date granted
   - Vendor account identifier/username
   - Permission set granted
   - Rotation tier
6) Add user to quarterly access review roster.

## 10. Offboarding and access removal
Triggers:
- Employee departure
- Role change (no longer working on marketplace)
- Vendor portal access unused for >90 days (unless exception approved)

Process:
1) Within **1 business day**, remove vendor portal access.
2) Remove user from the “Partner Portals (Restricted)” vault.
3) If the user had Tier 1 access, rotate relevant passwords immediately.
4) Document completion in the offboarding ticket.

## 11. Audit trail and evidence
### 11.1 Required logging
- Vendor portal activity logs (where available) must be retained per vendor defaults; screenshots/export of logs may be required for audits or incident response.
- Redwood must maintain an internal record of:
  - Who submitted/published a change (ticket reference)
  - What was changed (link to draft, copy doc, or PRD reference)
  - Who approved it (names + date)

### 11.2 Evidence storage
- Evidence artifacts (e.g., vendor log exports, submission confirmations) are stored in the restricted GRC evidence drive and referenced from the ticket.
- Security/compliance evidence shared with vendors must follow the “Marketplace Security Packet Evidence Index” rules (NDA gating where required).

## 12. Submitting listing changes (change management)
### 12.1 Required pre-submit checks
Before submitting any change for vendor review/publish:
- Confirm copy aligns with the approved “marketplace messaging framework” and avoids unverified security claims.
- Confirm SKU naming matches the ADR for SKU naming and entitlement IDs.
- Confirm screenshots are current and redacted as needed.
- Confirm the Marketplace Review Checklist is completed for the change type.

### 12.2 Submission workflow (standard)
1) Create/associate a tracking ticket (Internal Support or project tracking) for the submission.
2) Collect approvals (Section 5.3).
3) Submit changes in vendor portal using an authorized submitter account.
4) Post submission confirmation (non-sensitive) to the tracking ticket:
   - Vendor submission ID (if provided)
   - Timestamp
   - Summary of changes
5) Track vendor feedback and resubmissions in the same ticket.

### 12.3 Emergency changes
Emergency = listing is broken, materially misleading, or blocks customer onboarding/procurement.
- Authorized: Full Submitter + Security approver.
- Follow-up: retrospective within 5 business days documenting root cause and any process gaps.

## 13. Quarterly access review
Owner: Olga Petrov (GRC)

Cadence: first week of each quarter.

Steps:
1) Export current access list from AWS/GCP portals (or manually verify if export not available).
2) Compare against the Authorized Personnel list (Section 5.2).
3) Validate MFA enrollment for each active user.
4) Remove any stale users and rotate Tier 1 credentials if any admin changes occurred.
5) Record review outcome (pass/fail, removals, rotations) in the quarterly Vendor Access Review record.

## 14. Exceptions
Exceptions require written approval from:
- Marcus Lin (Security Engineering) AND
- Olga Petrov (GRC)

Examples:
- Vendor portal does not support security keys and requires TOTP.
- Vendor requires a shared admin account due to portal limitation.

Exception records must include compensating controls (e.g., additional monitoring, shorter rotation cadence).

## 15. Appendix A — Quick reference tables
### A1) Access/approval matrix (summary)
- Copy/assets edits → Approvals: PMM + Marketing; Submitter: Copy/Assets or Full
- Pricing/SKU/metering → Approvals: Product + Finance + Legal; Submitter: Full
- Security packet language/evidence → Approvals: Security + GRC; Submitter: Full
- Payout/tax/banking → Approvals: Finance + Legal + Security; Submitter: Seller Profile/Finance Admin

### A2) Rotation schedule (summary)
- Tier 1 (payout/tax): 60 days
- Tier 2 (listing submission): 90 days
- Tier 3 (view-only): 180 days
